question: Who was the twenty-fourth Jain Tirthankara?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahavira**, also known as **Vardhamana**, is recognized as the **twenty-fourth and last Tirthankara of Jainism**.
 
• He was born in **599 BCE **in **Kundagram, Bihar, India**.
 
• Mahavira attained kevala jnana (omniscience) after 12 years of rigorous penance.
 
• He preached the principles of **Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-possession)**.
 
• Mahavira's teachings form the core of Jain philosophy and are compiled in the Agamas, the canonical scriptures of Jainism.
 
• He is considered a reformer who revitalized and reorganized the Jain community during his lifetime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rishabha**

 
 
• He is considered the **first Tirthankara in Jainism**.
 
• Rishabha is believed to have lived millions of years ago, and his teachings laid the foundation for the Jain tradition.
 
 
 
• **Parshvanatha**
 
 
• He is the **twenty-third Tirthankara in Jainism**.
 
• Parshvanatha is known for advocating the fourfold restraint (Chaturyama) – non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, and non-possession.
